E: Panel E is an outlet view showing fractures involving the posterior iliac wing and pubic rami.

in_text_mentions: The initial diagnosis of an acetabular fracture was made from the antero-posterior pelvic X-ray (Figure 1). Judet views and 3D CT demonstrated a fracture of the anterior column with a fracture line in the iliac wing and involvement of the SI joint (Figure 2). The fracture line in the weight bearing dome extended to the SI joint without involving the posterior column and this was an unusual type of acetabular fracture. In spite of continuity of the posterior column, the whole acetabulum was detached from the ilium, as the fracture entered the SI joint.

Because of severe fractures and dislocation, femoral head was blocked by the posterior margin of acetabulum. After recognizing the irreducibility and severity, we opted for emergency surgical intervention.
